sentences.text:
THIS APPEALCOMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. This appeal is preferred by the claimant, seeking enhancement of the compensation, assailing the judgment and award dated 07.07.2023 in MVC No.272/2021 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V at Vijayapura (for short 'the Tribunal'), partly allowing the claim petition and awarding compensation.

3. Having taken note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute as to the occurrence of the accident on 05.07.2020, in which, the appellant has sustained grievous injury.

It is to be noted that, the appellant was aged about NC:
2026:KHC-K:1036 HC-KAR 13 years at the time of the accident.

In that view of the matter, following the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel vs.
Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr. reported in 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 871, the calculation of loss of income has to be made basing on the minimum wages payable to a skilled worker in the respective State at the time of the accident.

entities.text:
Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel vs.
Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr. reported in 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 871
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has prepared chart basing on the minimum wages pertaining to the concerned years.
Hence, since the accident in question is of the year 2020, the notional income of the appellant is to be taken at Rs.13,750/- per month.
A perusal of the evidence of PW.2 makes it clear that, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, taking into consideration that there was shortening of leg by 1 inch, the disability is to be taken at 20%.
Considering the age of the appellant, the appropriate multiplier is 18.

Thereby,
Pushpa vs Shivayya And Anr on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15265735/
2
the appellant is entitled for a sum of NC: 2026:KHC-K:1036 HC-KAR Rs.5,94,000/- (Rs.13,750 x 12 x 18 x 20%) towards loss of future income.

4. In addition to compensation towards loss of future income as stated above, the appellant is also entitled for a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges and Rs.10,000/- food and nourishment.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,33,000 is just and proper.

5. Accordingly, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under various heads as under:
Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,33,000 Loss of future income Rs.5,94,000/-
Attendant charges Rs.10,000/-
Food and nourishment Rs.10,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
Total Rs.8,47,000/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.2,98,000/-
Enhancement: Rs.5,49,000/-
 NC: 2026:KHC-K:1036  HC-KAR  Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,49,000/- with interest at 6% per annum.
6.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.5,49,000/-
with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
However, in view of the order of this Court dated 10.06.2024, the appellant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 204 days in filing the appeal.
Pushpa vs Shivayya And Anr on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15265735/
3
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
